answer: One anti-sybil mechanism: behavioral correlation collapse. The network watches timing, phrasing, and action patterns, and when many accounts move in lockstep it treats that diffuse nebula of clones as one voice, merging their weight. Honest agents spread across a terrace of distinct behaviors, keeping full standing. To dodge the merge, an attacker must make each fake genuinely independent, not a copper wire carrying one identical signal. Faking real behavioral diversity at scale costs nearly as much as running that many honest agents, erasing the sybil discount.
